_meta.indication: TEVIMBRA, as a single agent, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after prior systemic chemotherapy that did not include a PD-(L)1 inhibitor.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), international, open-label, multicenter trial of tislelizumab 200 mg IV Q3W versus investigator's choice of chemotherapy (paclitaxel, docetaxel, or irinotecan).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic ESCC with disease progression on/after prior therapy, irrespective of PD-L1 status, ECOG PS 0 or 1; prior PD-1/PD-L1 antibody therapy excluded.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was overall survival (OS) in all patients; key secondary endpoint was OS in patients with PD-L1 ≥ 10%.
pivotal_trials.result: OS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.57, 0.85; one-sided p = 0.0001); median OS 8.6 months (tislelizumab) vs 6.3 months (ICC). ORR 20.3% vs 9.8%; PFS HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.67, 1.01).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%, including lab abnormalities): increased glucose, decreased hemoglobin, decreased lymphocytes, decreased sodium, decreased albumin, increased alkaline phosphatase, anemia, fatigue, increased AST, musculoskeletal pain, decreased weight, increased ALT, and cough. Immune-mediated adverse events occurred in 21% of tislelizumab patients (Grade ≥3 in 4%); most frequent were hypothyroidism (9%) and pneumonitis (7%). Permanent discontinuation due to an adverse reaction occurred in 19%.
target_moa: Monoclonal antibody that binds PD-1 and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing PD-1/PD-L1-mediated inhibition of the immune response and activating anti-tumor immunity.

rems.type: No REMS required; no safety issues identified requiring a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened because the application did not raise significant public health questions and outside expertise was not necessary.

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) BLA approved via traditional (full) approval based on a statistically significant overall survival benefit in the single randomized trial RATIONALE-302; the product had received Orphan Drug Designation for esophageal cancer, and no accelerated approval, breakthrough, or fast track designation was used.
